newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint eases vs dlr, BCE mark futures up.
newsitem.headline: Forint eases vs dlr, BCE mark futures up.

text.p: End-of-month currency buying drove the forint further away from the central bank's bid, traders said on Thursday, adding the gap should close in a few days.
"This cannot last as treasury bills and bonds remain attractive," said Balazs Benczedi of West LB Hungaria.
The forint closed at 170.15/20 against the U.S. unit compared with an opening 169.90/95, while the gap that separated the forint from the central bank bid was 45 to 50 pips.

On the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) mark futures rose for all but one maturity, with the German mark being the favourite of the day, accounting for 7,653 contracts of a total 18,924 contracts or 2.38 billion forints turnover.
The dollar, which dropped for most maturities and levelled for only one, was the second most traded with some 4,500 contracts.
Lira and Ecu futures were steady except one Ecu maturity, the sterling and the Swiss franc ended mixed and the yen rose for three maturities.
